key_insight: UniMem learns to route streaming tasks into either episodic retrieval or expandable parametric memory, helping LLM agents stay stable on recurring patterns while remaining plastic for new ones.
engineering_relevance: For autonomous engineering workflows, this offers a practical way to retain and reuse reliable execution strategies over long, boundary-agnostic task streams without requiring explicit task labels.
method: Learnable routing tokens act as memory controllers.
Novel or sparse tasks are stored in an episodic buffer for retrieval-augmented execution.
Recurring and reliable patterns are consolidated into expandable parametric memory blocks.
evidence_signal: In long-horizon streaming task evaluations across three backbone models, UniMem improved performance by an average of 4.0 EM points over baselines.
watch_item: The approach adds routing and memory-management complexity, so its efficiency and robustness will depend on how well the controller generalizes and how memory growth is bounded in deployment.
paper_title: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams
